citation: Coyne, M. D., Little, M., Rawlinson, D., Simmons, D., Kwok, O., Kim, M., Simmons, L., Hagan-Burke, S., & Civetelli, C. (2013). Replicating the impact of a supplemental beginning reading intervention: The role of instructional context. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 6(1), 1-23. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2012.706694
report_number: JREE 6(1):1-23; DOI 10.1080/19345747.2012.706694 (ERIC EJ994735). IES-funded ('Project Early Reading Intervention'). Evaluates the commercial Early Reading Intervention (ERI; Pearson/Scott Foresman, 2004) curriculum delivered by teachers trained by the research team, vs a school-designed typical-practice intervention (SDI).
design: Cluster RCT (varied replication study). Assignment level = Teacher/Class: all kindergarten classrooms in 10 elementary schools in one central-Florida district were randomly assigned within schools to ERI (n=25 classes) or SDI (n=23 classes), total 48 classes / 162 at-risk kindergarten students (ERI n=87, SDI n=75 at posttest). Subject = beginning reading/early literacy. Grade = kindergarten (K). Low-SES, mostly Title I schools. The COMPARISON is an ACTIVE comparison (school-designed typical-practice reading intervention, also 30 min/day small-group, ~equivalent sessions), NOT business-as-usual / no-treatment. Analyzed with 3-level HLM (students within interventionists within schools), ANCOVA-style covariates (matched pretest, PPVT, age, gender, ethnicity, special-ed, ELL). Reported effect sizes are Hedges' delta_w (Hedges, 2007), cluster-corrected.
problems: ACTIVE-COMPARISON FLAG: the comparison condition is NOT business-as-usual/no-treatment. It is a 'school-designed intervention' (SDI) -- an alternative active supplemental reading intervention delivered to at-risk kindergartners for the same 30 min/day in small groups for an equivalent number of sessions. The paper notes the SDI teachers had previously received extensive PD in evidence-based reading and used FCRR resources, so this is a strong active comparator (and indeed it outperformed ERI in the replication). The meta-analysis spec assumes TPD-vs-business-as-usual, so these contrasts may not meet that comparison criterion. Registry row 20 codes 'One' effect size, but the experimental replication contrast (ERI vs SDI, replication study) reports 8 separate reading/early-literacy outcomes; all 8 are extracted (central logic can aggregate/select). The study's headline finding is NULL: HLM revealed NO statistically significant ERI-vs-SDI differences on any measure in the replication study (most point estimates slightly favor SDI). All 8 outcomes are pretest- and covariate-adjusted standardized norm-referenced instruments (WRMT-R/NU, CTOPP, DIBELS) -- i.e. standardized_independent, despite the registry tagging the study's TPD trainer as 'Res/Dev' (that field refers to who delivered the PD, not the test type). The paper does NOT report a standard error / variance for the Hedges' delta_w values, so g_se and g_var are left null. Per-measure ICCs are not reported for the replication study; the paper gives only across-measure ranges (group-level ICC .16-.32; school-level ICC .06-.22), so n_clusters is recorded but icc is left null (not guessed). g is taken directly from Table 10 (authors' Hedges' delta_w, cluster-adjusted); impact_estimate is the raw HLM group-difference coefficient gamma_010 from Table 7 (raw outcome-score units, NOT standardized).
